prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2015 manifesto is a call to “believe in Britain”: restore sovereignty, control borders, spend taxpayers’ money at home first, and make politics answer to the people—not Brussels, big government or big corporations. It pledges fully costed change without raising taxes, cutting vital services or adding to the national debt, funded by leaving the EU, reducing foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula, ending health tourism and cutting government waste.

Economy and tax
- Leave the EU to save £9bn net a year; reform the Barnett Formula; scrap HS2; cut Whitehall/QUANGO waste.
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000 (no income tax on the minimum wage); introduce a 30% band and lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable allowances for married couples/civil partners.
- Cut small business rates 20% up to £50k rateable value; crack down on late payment; pilot trade credit insurance access.
- Restore tax sovereignty, close multinational avoidance, and zero‑rate VAT on listed‑building repairs and sanitary products.

Immigration and borders
- “Immigration is about space, not race.” Leave the EU to end free movement; introduce an Australian‑style points system; five‑year moratorium on unskilled migration; cap highly skilled work visas at 50,000; +2,500 Border Agency staff and exit/entry checks; no amnesty; deport foreign criminals; five‑year wait for full benefits/NHS access beyond urgent care. EU citizens legally resident at the referendum can stay.

NHS and social care
- Extra £12bn for the NHS over five years; 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; free hospital parking; GP pilots in A&E; +£1.5bn for mental health/dementia; end PFI; “licence to manage” for NHS managers; abolish Monitor/CQC, replace with locally elected county health boards.
- End health tourism; NHS is national, not international.
- Restore social care funding (+£1.2bn/yr), integrate health and social care, dignity code, end 15‑minute visits; raise Carer’s Allowance.

Energy and environment
- Repeal the Climate Change Act and scrap green levies/EU ETS to cut bills; back nuclear, shale and coal; end subsidies for onshore wind/large solar; support hydro; keep the lights on.

Transport and housing
- Scrap HS2; oppose road‑pricing and EU eCall; end most tolls; safety‑led camera use only; fair HGV levy for foreign trucks.
- Build on brownfield with a national register, remediation grants and stamp duty relief; bring empty homes into use; prioritise locals for social housing; bar non‑citizens from Help to Buy/Right to Buy (armed forces exception); protect green belt; local referenda on major developments.

Education and families
- More school choice including grammar and vocational routes; abolish KS1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; first‑aid in PSHE; reverse special‑school closures.
- No tuition fees for UK students in STEMM who work/tax in the UK for five years; drop the 50% HE target.
- Deregulate childcare to boost places and cut costs; wrap‑around school care 8am–6pm; presume 50/50 shared parenting; strengthen child protection.

Welfare and pensions
- Scrap the bedroom tax; keep housing benefit for under‑25s; GP‑led disability assessments; foodbank advisers; limit new child benefit to two children and stop payments abroad; raise Carer’s Allowance; flexible state‑pension window; ban pension cold‑calling; lifelong war widows’ pensions.

Law, order and defence
- Leave the ECHR; British Bill of Rights; restore “innocent until proven guilty”; more frontline police/prison/border staff; tough on trafficking, grooming, FGM and forced marriage; decriminalise TV‑licence non‑payment.
- Spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; renew Trident; rebuild forces; oppose an EU army; income‑tax relief while on active service.

Farming, fishing, culture and democracy
- UK farm payments focused on family farms; strong animal welfare (ban live exports, CCTV in abattoirs).
- Leave the CFP; 12‑mile and 200‑mile UK control; back under‑10m boats and sea angling.
- Celebrate British values; English for official documents; free speech within the law; St George’s and St David’s Days as bank holidays.
- Political reform: citizens’ initiative referendums, real recall (20%), open primaries, proportional voting, end postal voting on demand, and local binding referenda on major planning. Trade policy returned to the UK via WTO seat and bespoke deals after Brexit.
